hints.title: Use each elevation as a maximum for a row of positions
hints.body: The plan identifies five occupied positions arranged in an L. In each viewing direction, an elevation shows the greatest stack height along that line of sight.
hints.recap: A plan shows positions; an elevation can hide cubes behind other cubes.
hints.pitfall: Do not add the visible cubes in the two elevations: many are the same cubes.
hints.pause: Mark the heights forced at the four positions away from the L-corner.

recall.reminder: Combine plans and elevations to recover three-dimensional constraints.

hints.title: Recover unhidden positions
hints.body: At each non-corner position, use the viewing direction that isolates it to mark all its occupied layers.
hints.recap: An unobstructed view fixes the occupancy of a position.
hints.pitfall: Check the layer pattern, not just its maximum height.
hints.pause: Determine the fixed cubes while leaving the corner unresolved.

recall.reminder: An unobstructed view fixes the occupancy of a position.

hints.title: Test the corner layers
hints.body: Check each possible corner layer against both elevations and the face-connection requirement.
hints.recap: A cube is optional only when every view and connectivity are preserved.
hints.pitfall: A missing lower corner cube may disconnect the arms.
hints.pause: Enumerate the permitted corner arrangements and total their cubes.

recall.reminder: A cube is optional only when every view and connectivity are preserved.

solution:
The plan has five occupied positions. The four non-corner stacks have fixed heights 2, 1, 3 and 1, giving seven cubes.

At the L-corner, the bottom cube must be present so that the arms are connected by faces. A second cube can be present without changing either elevation. A third cube would make one elevation too high.

Thus the corner contributes either one or two cubes, giving totals 7+1=8 or 7+2=9. Answer F: 8 or 9.
knowledgePattern: Reconstruct optional voxels from three orthographic views
